results.title: Mother, 2 children found dead inside car in Bulacan
results.description: A woman and her two young children were found dead inside a car in a remote vacant lot in Barangay Talacsan, San Rafael, Bulacan, on Thursday afternoon, Aug. 20. Police said they received a report at 2:11 p.m. from a concerned citizen about a suspicious silver vehicle abandoned in the area. Authorities immediately responded and, upon checking the vehicle, were shocked to discover three bodies in the back of the multipurpose vehicle (MPV). Police said the victims were residents of Baliwag City. The father told investigators he last saw his family at 5:00 p.m. on Wednesday, Aug. 19. The mother was 31 years old, while the children were aged nine and four. The Philippine National Police Forensic Group is conducting a thorough investigation into the incident. As of press time, authorities have not yet determined the cause of death.

results.title: Prolight + Sound Bangkok debut set to energise Southeast Asia's pro AV and entertainment technology market
results.description: BANGKOK, Aug. 21, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Prolight + Sound, the renowned international trade fair brand for professional AV, lighting, music, and entertainment technology, will make its Bangkok debut this year with the launch of Prolight + Sound Bangkok (PLSB), a new regional meeting point for the industry. Taking place from 30 September - 2 October 2026 at the Bangkok International Trade & Exhibition Centre, the show will unite international brands and key Southeast Asian players to accelerate market entry, partnerships, and the adoption of cutting‐edge solutions across the region's booming entertainment, music, events, MICE, and tourism sectors. The show will feature six technology zones covering the breadth of the entertainment and pro AV industries Over 150 international exhibitors and more than 5,000 trade visitors are projected to attend. Companies from eleven countries and regions have confirmed their participation including France, Germany, Hong Kong, India, Italy, Mainland China, Malaysia, Singapore, Switzerland, Thailand, and the UK. The growing exhibitor lineup includes established brands such as ACME, Altimate, Big Dipper, Botai, CJS, DJ Power, ETC, Faital Pro, Giant Truss, Gis AG, Golden Duck, HK Audio, ICE Prosound, IMAGE AV, MARANI, Mission T, Neutrik, N‐Labs, PENN ELCOM, Pharos Architectural Controls, Reyn Audio, Roxtone, Silver Star, Sixty82 Doughty Asia, Tycoon, VL Audio, and Yoda. A dedicated Singapore Pavilion, organised by the Pro Audiovisual & Lighting Integration Association of Singapore (AVLIAS), featuring leading companies like Acoustic & Lighting System, EP‐Tec Solutions, MA Lighting, New Wave Display, Robe Lighting, Total Solution Marketing, and Unearthed Productions, underscores Singapore's strong regional commitment. What exhibitors are saying about show participation Rising opportunities across Southeast Asia's live events and entertainment sectors position PLSB as a strategic gateway. ACME's Sales Director, Yanqiang Yang, stated: "We aim to connect directly with regional distributors and end‐users, showcasing our latest products for hands‐on evaluation." HK Audio's Chief Sales Officer, Christian Jordan, commented: "As Southeast Asia continues to experience strong growth, this trade show offers HK Audio a strategic platform to strengthen our regional presence. We are confident PLSB will develop into a key business hub." Connecting global expertise with regional growth The show's comprehensive fringe programme includes a Drum Circle & Music Therapy Experience Workshop in partnership with IQ PLUS Music, Serenity Sound, and Tycoon, alongside sessions on AI, immersive experiences, concerts, and smart AV integration. An intensive three‐day masterclass by the Thailand Professional Qualification Institute (TPQI) will cover sound engineering, acoustic design, and live production. Meanwhile, AVLIAS will host the Future of the ASEAN Pro AVL, which will explore regional business opportunities and cross‐border collaboration, driving knowledge transfer and long‐term partnerships. Pre‐register now: https://prolight-sound-bangkok.hk.messefrankfurt.com/bangkok/en/planning-preparation/visitors/preregistration.html?utm_source=pressrelease&utm_medium=PRNewswire&utm_campaign=082026

results.title: Sean Duffy flops as viewers reject his much-delayed reality show: report
results.description: Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy has struggled to attract viewers to his controversial road trip reality show after months of delays. According to a Thursday report by MeidasTouch, "almost nobody is watching" Duffy's six-episode reality show, "Great American Road Trip," which features his wife and nine children traveling with him through several states. The show has been criticized for its questionable funding sources and for showing off Duffy's road trip vacation while Americans struggle to afford gas and groceries. The show aired on Wednesday, and after 24 hours, the six episodes had accumulated only about 5,400 views combined, according to MeidasTouch. The most-viewed episode was Duffy's Philadelphia episode, which had 2,300 views, and his Charleston and Arizona episodes drew fewer than 500 viewers each, MeidasTouch reported. Four of the six episodes had only 600 views, and the most-viewed episode had only 59 likes, MeidasTouch added. Comments for the videos have also been turned off, MeidasTouch added. Duffy spent months promoting the reality show as a celebration of America's 250th birthday. It was originally supposed to premiere in June, but it was delayed until this week. CNN reported that the nonprofit Great American Road Trip, Inc . covered production costs, including filming, crew, food, fuel, lodging, and activities. The Department of Transportation accepted the nonprofit covering the cost as a gift, according to CNN. The Great American Road Trip nonprofit has come under fire because it was funded with millions from companies that the Department of Transportation is supposed to regulate, including Boeing, Toyota, United Airlines, Chase Travel, and the Royal Caribbean Group. The show was also slammed shortly after its airing, with CNN panelist Meghan Hays calling it "gross" on Thursday. Duffy, a former reality TV star, has defended the project as an effort to encourage Americans to travel and experience the country, MeidasTouch noted.

Eleanor Yeh: Etra Fine Jewellery and the Art of Meaningful Ownership
results.description: HONG KONG, Aug. 21, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- As part of JESSICA's women entrepreneurship story series, this interview was planned and conducted by the JESSICA team. We invited Eleanor Yeh, Founder and Creative Director of Etra Fine Jewellery, to share how she embraces "meaningful ownership" as her jewellery philosophy, connecting family heritage, sustainable design, and the lifestyle of modern women. Through Eleanor's entrepreneurial journey and brand story, JESSICA continues to spotlight inspiring women leaders, creative talents, and entrepreneurs, showcasing their vision, perseverance, and influence across different fields. Eleanor Yeh: Etra Fine Jewellery and the Art of Meaningful Ownership Read more at: https://www.jessicahk.com/global/eleanor-yeh-etra-fine-jewellery Inside thousands of high-security bank vaults across Hong Kong, countless pieces of inherited jewellery sit untouched in the dark. Millions of dollars in gold and ancestral gemstones are locked away inside steel safety deposit boxes, too sentimental to sell, yet too out of sync with contemporary lifestyles. To Eleanor Yeh, founder and creative director of Etra Fine Jewellery, these pieces represent an invisible archive of trapped stories waiting to be told. From her Hong Kong atelier, she is helping clients transform old jewellery into pieces that feel personal, wearable, and meaningful again through bespoke design and heirloom remodelling. The Chemistry of Skinship What separates fine jewellery from other objects of material luxury is its physical intimacy. While a painting hangs on a wall and an architectural monument is viewed from a distance, jewellery is meant to be lived in. "Jewellery's different, because it's against our body," Eleanor explains. It warms through wear, balances on the finger, and moves in rhythm with daily life. When a piece of jewellery fails to connect emotionally, it is inevitably exiled to a life in storage. Eleanor wants to make sure that does not happen. By stepping away from mass-produced, one-size-fits-all designs, she invites clients to become partners in the creative process. Under her guidance, jewellery becomes a vessel of memories, identity, and the stories people choose to carry with them through life. Eleanor Yeh: Etra Fine Jewellery and the Art of Meaningful Ownership A Life Lived Across Horizons Born in Taiwan, Eleanor moved to the United Kingdom for middle school, spending two decades absorbing British traditions. After graduating from university, she spent ten years working within the high-stakes front office of an investment bank. A relocation to Tokyo for her husband's career required her to resign, initiating a ten-year chapter as a stay-at-home mother. As her children grew older, a sense of restlessness prompted a desire to re-enter the professional world, leading her to eventually establish her atelier in Hong Kong. This multi-chaptered background has provided Eleanor with an international perspective that avoids superficial "East-meets-West" design clichés. Instead, she draws on the distinct philosophies of each place she has called home. Her two decades in the UK instilled a deep appreciation for classic, enduring structures, while her years in Tokyo introduced her to the aesthetic power of wabi-sabi, the Japanese philosophy centred on restraint, balance, and the belief that less is more. Eleanor's actual path into the jewellery industry was equally unique, shaped by a mix of analytical science and creative curiosity. Before she ever designed her first piece, her education and early career in finance were heavily rooted in analytical and structured thinking. Her eventual desire to re-enter the professional world led her back to a creative spark from childhood. Growing up, her father was an avid art collector. While he favoured austere, black-and-white ink paintings, Eleanor found herself captivated by his collection of decorative arts, which was filled with vibrant jade, amethyst, and colourful tourmalines. When she decided to transition into jewellery, she naturally leaned on her structured, analytical background rather than a purely creative one. This logical approach made gemmology the perfect bridge for her varied background. To build a rigorous framework for her curiosity, she studied Asian art history at SOAS, became a GIA Graduate Gemmologist, and later combined this scientific foundation with formal design studies. It was this distinct marriage of technical precision, global exposure, and artistic vision that earned her the 2024 Gianmaria Buccellati Foundation Award for Excellence in Jewellery Design, a global honour won for an intricate design inspired by the architecture of the Basilica di Santa Croce during her travels to Italy. Today, Eleanor calls Hong Kong home, drawn by the city's intense energy and unmatched position in the global trade. She draws on her own layered background to help her equally well-travelled clients translate their own experiences into timeless pieces. "Hong Kong is probably the best place to be in Asia," she says. "It's very energetic and stressful at the same time, but it gives you that motivation to keep pushing." Eleanor Yeh: Etra Fine Jewellery and the Art of Meaningful Ownership The Core of Sustainability At the core of Etra's philosophy is a rejection of the "buy-and-discard" mentality that permeates modern consumption. Eleanor champions meaningful ownership, encouraging individuals to look inward and evaluate their true needs. In Etra's remodelling service, client heirlooms are carefully disassembled. The gold is weighed and sold to specialised gold refiners who return it to local artisan workshops. The value of this recycled gold is then credited back to the client's budget toward a new design, while gems are reset and reused. This circular process allows clients to transform old possessions into functional, modern designs without wasting raw resources. Eleanor recalls a recent project for a finance executive who owned an old suite of heavy, outdated jewellery featuring blue sapphires and diamonds from her mother. The client wanted a practical piece she could wear every day to her corporate office. Eleanor unmounted the stones, recycled the gold, and engineered a sleek, graduated necklace using the central sapphires and diamonds. The client now wears it daily, and leftover stones remain available for future pieces. "We're keeping the memory alive," Eleanor says. "And if she passes it on to her daughter, that memory continues perpetually." This philosophy is one Eleanor models in her personal life and passes down to her own children. She openly reflects on her own past mistakes of purchasing dozens of fast-fashion accessories, only to realize that the total cost could have been used to acquire a few high-quality, timeless investments. "Because we have so many choices, we don't know how to make choices," she says. "You have to ask yourself the questions about what is really useful...to buy design with tomorrow in mind." Eleanor Yeh: Etra Fine Jewellery and the Art of Meaningful Ownership The Architecture of Trust Because heirloom remodelling requires dismantling an object of immense sentimental and financial value, Eleanor's business operates on an architecture of trust. Every project begins with conversation. She meets clients to understand their lifestyle, personality, and story before any design work starts. "My objective is to understand the client," she explains. She deliberately considers the long-term utility of a piece. "Depending on their needs and lifestyle, I try to create something which will stay with them, stay relevant, and evolve." This focus on functionality is evident across all of Etra's commissions. When a gentleman recently approached Eleanor to design an engagement ring for his partner, a professional athlete with a demanding training schedule, Eleanor spent hours analysing the recipient's active lifestyle as an athlete and trainer. The final design was simple, secure, and specifically engineered to withstand rigorous physical activity while maintaining an elegant, minimalist aesthetic. Intangible Values Over the years, Eleanor's own understanding of luxury has shifted. It is no longer defined by status or price tags, but rather by quality and a care for the environment. This philosophy is exactly why she has no plans to scale Etra into a massive, corporate brand. Instead, she chooses to stay agile and focused, dedicating herself entirely to individual stories and preservation. For Eleanor, the real reward of this slow, intentional process occurs when a client sees and wears their completed piece for the first time. Seeing that connection is what makes the entire journey worthwhile. The ultimate goal is simply for them to wear it with confidence, happiness and joy. "When their faces light up, that's my job done," she smiles. About JESSICA Since 2000, JESSICA has been dedicated to empowering women by curating and reporting on the latest trends, celebrity fashion, business insights, lifestyle, art and cultural content. It also established the Most Successful Women Awards to honour outstanding women across business, technology, the arts, sports, social service and other sectors, recognising their achievements and contributions. Through its extended platform, JES Network, JESSICA continues to inspire and connect influential women leaders and the next generation around the world. In addition, JESSICA actively supports local sports, youth and women's development through the JESSICA Charitable Foundation, bringing more positive energy to the community. for a severe El Niño season President Trump added to the week's Iran headlines on Thursday, telling WABC Radio that Tehran's capacity to produce missiles and drones has fallen sharply compared with five months ago. He described Iran as being in bad shape, citing inflation running near 300 percent and a currency he called virtually valueless, while reiterating that Iran will not be permitted to obtain a nuclear weapon. The comments came alongside a separate report that a senior Iranian official is preparing an economic warfare strategy of its own, aimed at using oil markets to pressure Trump ahead of November's midterm elections. The plan reportedly includes strikes on Gulf bypass terminals in Saudi Arabia and the UAE, along with efforts to shut down the flow of oil moving through the Strait of Hormuz via the US backed shadow fleet, with the explicit aim of pushing pump prices higher before the vote. Against that backdrop, oil prices held near recent highs in otherwise steady trade. In Japan, data released Friday showed core consumer inflation rose 1.8 percent in July from a year earlier, matching forecasts and adding to the case for the Bank of Japan to raise rates at its September policy meeting. The yen struggled to gain traction on the back of the data, with USD/JPY straddling the 159.00 level, though the currency lost more ground against other major crosses than it did against the dollar itself. Elsewhere in currency markets, the euro, sterling, the New Zealand dollar and the Australian dollar all traded higher against the greenback, with several sitting near their strongest levels in recent months as investors continued to question the durability of the US Treasury's efforts to manage bond yields. Regional equities were mixed. Japan's Nikkei was on track for its worst week in more than a month, down around 4 percent, as rising oil prices and elevated bond yields weighed on sentiment amid the escalating Middle East standoff. The broader Topix was set for a weekly decline of roughly 3.5 percent. South Korea's KOSPI told a different story intraday, opening sharply lower before reversing to trade higher as chipmakers tracked overnight gains among US peers, though the index remained on course for a weekly loss of around 1 percent. On the policy front, China's Vice Finance Minister Liao Min said Beijing will introduce additional fiscal support in a timely manner, pledging to maintain policy continuity while allocating resources over a longer cycle, as the world's second largest economy shows signs of a broadening slowdown. Separately, the Panama Canal Authority said it will cap daily vessel transits from early September, reversing an earlier pledge not to restrict passage, as it prepares for what it expects to be a longer and more severe El Niño season than in past years. This article was written by Eamonn Sheridan at investinglive.com.
